key_insight: A backwards, data-driven link from optimized metallic microstructure and texture to the underlying alloy recipe is learnable, and simple conventional descriptors outperform learned embeddings for this small magnesium dataset.
engineering_relevance: This supports inverse design workflows for alloy development by helping infer likely composition and extrusion settings from a target microstructure when expert intuition is limited.
method: Built an in-house dataset of 107 magnesium alloy extrusion conditions across 14 alloys with optical micrographs and X-ray texture measurements.
Compared three representations of structure: conventional grain/texture statistics, a pretrained vision embedding, and a graph neural network on the grain network.
Used prediction heads for two inverse tasks: predict alloy composition from process conditions and predict process parameters from composition.
evidence_signal: Under 5-fold cross-validation, conventional descriptors identified the correct alloy in 65% of held-out cases versus 17% for majority-class guessing, while learned embeddings stayed below 30%; adding microstructure roughly halved temperature error for process prediction.
watch_item: The dataset is small and highly discrete, so the results may not generalize well and order-aware classification heads may be more reliable than free-value regression.
paper_title: Which alloy composition,what process parameters? Inferring the recipe from optimized metallic microstructure and texture
